correctness.rationale: For a,b,s>=1 the bipartite adjacency matrix satisfies A^3=ab A and A^4=ab A^2. Matrix Cayley-Hamilton over integer polynomial ring gives q_{t+1}(z)=(z+2)q_t(z)-q_{t-1}(z) and p_t=(q_t-q_{t-1}-1)/z. Exact T^t-I block expression reduces identity mod 2^s to simultaneous divisibility 2^s|q_t(z) and 2^s|gcd(a,b)p_t(z), so collapsing to a 2x2 z-only cat map would be incorrect. Explicit factorization and parity gives base orders 2,4,3 with exact valuation anchors; binomial lifting from h>=2 gives one extra 2-adic valuation per squaring. This proves all five arithmetic regimes with odd z=3 mod4 s=1 boundary. T is invertible shear product so all states are periodic, and a finite group cannot be union of two proper kernels, giving some primitive cycle of full matrix order. Independent modular exponentiation checked 150 cases a,b<=5,s<=6 and distinguished K1,4 from K2,2 although same ab=4.
